title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Chapter VI, 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)', June 1986. Grothendieck is setting up an axiomatic framework for tame ('modérée') topology. The basic data are a set 𝓕 of 'figures' (stratified, tame subsets of a space). Inside it sit distinguished subsets: 𝓛 (the 'lieux') and 𝓜 (apparently the figures with a single stratum, since a member of 𝓜 lying below F is called a stratum of F). The data are organised as an 'atelier'. The previous page introduced the shadow and the 'multiombre' of a figure, indexed by its set of strata F̃.

This page lists the canonical structure.

(1.10) Three partial orders on 𝓕:
- G ≤ F, 'G is a sub-figure of F'. If G = X ∈ 𝓜, then X is a stratum of F.
- G ≪ F, 'G is a refinement of F'. If G = X ∈ 𝓜, X is an element of (probably) the open part, or the set of open strata, of F.
- G ≼ F, 'G is a subdivision of F'. In modern terms, G is a finer stratification with the same underlying set.

(1.11) ≤ and ≪ restrict to meaningful orders on 𝓜. The induced ≼ on 𝓜 is called less significant as a structure.

Margin notes:
- G ≪ F ⇒ G ≤ F, so every refinement is a sub-figure.
- The orders induced by ≤ and ≪ on 𝓛 reduce to equality. This matches the previous page ('se réduisant au =') and the next page (the relations are 'triviales sur L').

(1.12) Two further derived relations, both expressed through ≤:
- F and G are compatible iff {F,G} has an upper bound for ≤, i.e. they are sub-figures of a common figure.
- F and G are disjoint iff they are compatible and their infimum in 𝓕 is φ_F, the least element (the empty figure).
- Hence disjoint ⇒ compatible.

The next page proves (1.13) from the axioms. Two figures are disjoint iff their sets of open lieux are set-theoretically disjoint and every lieu of one is compatible with (indeed disjoint from) every lieu of the other.

Purpose: to set up the order-theoretic skeleton (posets of figures, strata, refinement, subdivision) of a 'tame topology' meant to replace point-set topology, in line with §5 of Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. Two definitional dependencies are left implicit.
The infimum of two compatible figures is used without saying here why it exists. Presumably an axiom of the atelier guarantees binary meets for bounded-above pairs, or meets in general.
The parenthetical identifications ('c'est donc une strate', 'élément de la gerbe/figure ouverte') depend on axioms stated on earlier pages, not on this page.

ideas.what: Three canonical partial orders on the set of tame 'figures': sub-figure (≤), refinement (≪, which implies ≤), and subdivision (≼).
ideas.modern_name: Posets of stratified (definable) sets under inclusion of stratified subspaces, open-union-of-strata inclusion, and refinement of stratifications
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather); cell decomposition in o-minimal geometry (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is announced programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme (1984, §5). This axiomatic order-theoretic set-up with figures, lieux and ateliers appears only in these unpublished notes, as far as I know.

ideas.what: Compatibility (bounded above) and disjointness (compatible with meet equal to the bottom element) as relations derived from the sub-figure order.
ideas.modern_name: Consistency / bounded-completeness (domain theory); disjointness as meet = ⊥ (orthogonality in posets and locales)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard order theory (Scott domains, frame/locale theory)

ideas.what: Restricted to the 'lieux' 𝓛, the orders ≤ and ≪ become trivial (equality). On the single-stratum figures 𝓜 they remain significant, while ≼ does not.
ideas.modern_name: Discreteness of the induced order on the minimal and atomic building blocks

missed.claim: This page belongs to an axiomatic, purely order-theoretic presentation of tame topology ('ateliers' of figures with orders ≤, ≪, ≼ and derived compatibility and disjointness). It is an alternative to o-minimality and to Shiota's or Kurdyka's axiomatics. It was not developed further in the literature. The definitions on this page alone are routine, but the framework as a whole remains unexplored.
missed.quote: Je note enfin autres relations importantes entre figures : F et G compatibles ... F et G disjoints
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This poset/atelier formalism is close to how one would build a site or locale-like structure on definable stratified sets. It could feed into modern work on constructible sheaves, exit paths and tame geometry. That is only true if the full axiom system of the notes is reconstructed; this page is just the definitions.

deep.surprise_reason: The page consists of definitions in a little-known unpublished axiomatisation of tame topology. Interest lies in the existence of the framework, not in any result on this page; the order-theoretic notions themselves are standard.
transcription_corrections: The first margin note most likely reads 'NB les relations d'ordre induites par ≤, ≪ sur 𝓛 sont =' (on the set of lieux 𝓛, not 𝓕). This is consistent with the previous page ('se réduisant au =') and the next page ('triviales sur L').
The second margin note reads: 'NB G ≪ F ⇒ G ≤ F, un raffinement de F est une sous-figure de F'.
In the ≤ line the correction is 'si G =X ∈ 𝓜' with 'G' struck and replaced by '=X'. The subsequent ≪ line reads 'si G = X ∈ 𝓜'.
The word read as 'gerbe [?]' in 'élément de la gerbe ouverte de F' is uncertain; 'figure ouverte' or 'partie ouverte' is also plausible from the image.
Last line ends 'F et G compatibles, et leur' (continued as 'inf dans F est φ_F' on the next page). The 'dans' before 'entre figures' is struck, as is 'deux'.
